title: Ravenwood Telemetry integration - call capture and next steps
content:
Meeting: Ravenwood telemetry integration intro (30m)
Date: 2026-02-24 10:00 PST (internal recap)
Attendees: Jordan Liu (RWI), Maya Ortiz (RWI), Samir Gupta (RWI), Tom Blake (Ravenwood - Eng Lead), Priya Shah (Ravenwood - DataOps)
Objective: capture Ravenwood production telemetry requirements and surface integration gotchas for Redwood Private VPC deployment. Draft plan for a small pilot (2-week PoC).

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Ravenwood wants private VPC deployment with tokenized telemetry sent to Redwood Console for per-route SLO dashboards.
- Primary concerns: PII in traces, ingest cost control, and <200ms 95th latency for inference calls.
- They will run a lightweight edge proxy in their subnet; want KV cache warmup behavior documented and a path for fallback to Hosted if Dedicated capacity is saturated.

Notes from conversation (raw):
- Tom: "We need to see latency per customer_org and per-model version. Billing side needs token counts by route."
- Priya: "We cannot send raw user messages off-net. We need masking / deterministic redaction before any telemetry leaves VPC. We can send hashed identifiers and token counts."
- Asked about certs/KMS: they have AWS KMS + internal HSM (Luna). They want KMS integration for key wrapping of telemetry blobs.
- They run Prometheus/Grafana internally and asked if we can push metrics to a pushgateway instead of pulling logs.
- They will be in us-east-1 and use c5n for edge proxies; expected inference fleet in dedicated g4dn/g5 pools.

Concrete requirements captured: (these will drive config for Private deployment)
1) Telemetry output must support obfuscation pipeline stage: options = [mask_user_text, hash_ids_sha256, strip_named_entities]. Default for PoC = hash_ids_sha256 + token_counts only.
2) Per-route token accounting exported as compressed daily blobs and per-request counts in sampling mode (1% sample) to Console.
3) Latency SLO: 95th <= 200ms for short completion requests (<64 tokens prompt + 32 tokens response) under baseline load (50 req/s sustained). Need test harness to validate.
4) Fallback policy: if Dedicated capacity < 60% health (per-node CPU/queue metrics), route to Hosted-compatible model (lower cost) with logging of fallback events.
5) KMS: Redwood should support encrypting telemetry export using customer KMS key (AES wrapping via AWS KMS).
6) Prometheus: expose route-level counters + histograms on /metrics; optionally push to provided Pushgateway endpoint behind auth token.

Gotchas / Risks (caller's voice):
- Priya: "If KV cache prewarming requires full prompt injection/external data, we can't send that data out of the VPC." -> Need alternative: local synthetic prompts for warmup or use cache replication snapshot method.
- Sampling vs aggregated export: they worry aggregated daily blobs lose fidelity for debugging. We need to keep traces for 7 days within VPC only; export samples offsite.
- Runtime versioning: Ravenwood rotates model versions fast (weekly). They want per-version health and rollout control in Console (canary + rollback). Feature exists but need to validate RBAC for their SREs.
- Cost sensitivity: telemetry ingestion spikes will be scrutinized. Add adjustable telemetry throttle and dry-run mode.

Initial technical proposal notes (draft):
- Deploy Private Control Plane in their us-east-1 account (customer-managed). Service mesh between redwood runtime and their edge proxy using mTLS; runtime writes per-request metrics to local Pushgateway and buffers encrypted export blobs to S3 with KMS key.
- Telemetry pipeline stages are chainable config blocks (mask/hash/filter/sample) in the Private deployment config. Default sample rate 1% but adjustable per-route via Console.
- Provide a small load-testing harness (k6 script + prompt generator) to simulate 50–200 req/s with latency assertions. Provide quickstart script to run inside their subnet.

Prompts / eval seeds Tom mentioned for latency testing (notes to self):
- small-completion: prompt ~30 tokens asking for JSON key-value; deterministic output expected.
- conversational-short: 3-turn conversation, last response <= 32 tokens.
- embedding-batch: 64 texts batched into single request (for parallelization test).

Action items / next steps (owner / eta):
- Jordan: draft PoC runbook + config template (telemetry pipeline + KMS example) — due 2026-03-03
- Maya: prototype Prometheus pushgateway integration sample and example metrics YAML — due 2026-03-05
- Samir: spin up k6 harness (scripts + sample prompts) and validate 95th latency under simulated 50 req/s on local G5 instance — due 2026-03-06
- Tom (Ravenwood): provide example prompt traces (redacted) + pointer to internal SSO group for RBAC testing — requested by 2026-03-04
- Priya (Ravenwood): confirm KMS key ARN / HSM constraints and whether export blobs are allowed to hit S3 (they prefer internal bucket) — due 2026-03-04
- Jordan/Maya: schedule 45m technical deep-dive with Ravenwood infra (include Eng + DataOps + Security) — propose 2026-03-08

Open questions (for follow-up):
- Can we support customer-managed pushgateway auth token rotation? (security team input)
- What is acceptable retention for raw traces inside VPC for debugging? (legal/privacy)
- If fallback to Hosted occurs, what PII policy applies to rerouted requests (they said no raw messages off-net) — need product/legal guidance on masked fallback payloads.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider adding an offline KV cache snapshot mechanism (serialize/transfer via S3 encrypted blob) to avoid sending real user prompts during warmup.
- Investigate offering a telemetry "dry-run" where pipeline runs but exports are blocked (only local metrics visible) so Ravenwood can estimate ingest before enabling exports.
- Add a Console feature flag for per-tenant telemetry sample rate with quick throttle UI.

Schedule / timeline (rough):
- Week 1 (PoC): install edge proxy, validate connectivity, run k6 harness, confirm metrics export to Pushgateway in VPC, verify KMS wrap flow.
- Week 2 (validation): test fallback behavior, run canary with 5% traffic to Hosted fallback, validate Console dashboards and RBAC.

Possible blockers:
- Security approval for pushing any hashed traces off-net. If blocked, still can do aggregated token counts but debugging will be harder.
- Ravenwood's HSM constraints may require an operator-level change to how we perform key wraps.

Next meeting: propose 2026-03-08 09:30 PST (45m) tech deep-dive. Prepare: PoC runbook draft, k6 script sample, Pushgateway example, KMS example.

Scratch / random bits (deleted later?):
- Quick command snippets for devs:
  - k6 run --vus 20 --duration 1m scripts/ravenwood_small_completions.js
  - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://pushgateway.ravenwood.internal/metrics/job/rw-inference

- Slack refs: #se-ravenwood-onramp, thread: thread-3f2c

End of capture.
